body: The ERR_CONNECT scenario cannot catch a taxonomy regression, so it does not actually prove what the seam's doc-comment claims ("originates from transport.ErrConnect through the real taxonomy — not a hand-built CodedError"). The production apply() path uses "ERR_CONNECT" as the *universal* fallback code for ANY deploy error (deployment_resource.go:599 -> diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_CONNECT", ...); diagSummary only overrides the fallback when errors.As finds an *engine.CodedError). Because the injected code and the fallback are the same string, this HasPrefix(summary, "[ERR_CONNECT] ") assertion passes even if wrapTransportErr dropped the CodedError entirely or classified it differently — the exact regression this scenario exists to guard. Strengthen it to distinguish the real path from the fallback, e.g. also assert the Detail carries the genuine dial text from the injected transport (s.createSummary check plus a check that the diagnostic Detail contains "connect: connection refused" / "dial tcp"), which can only reach the diagnostic via transport.ErrConnect -> wrapTransportErr, not via the hardcoded fallback.

The "RequiresReplace fires on immutable path <field>" outline covers only 4 of the 7 immutable paths DESIGN §5.2 (and immutableKey in deployment_resource.go:300-311) enumerate: it omits metadata.name, pattern.install_root, and role_name. Since immutableKey is a single join over all 7 positions, a regression that drops any of the three uncovered fields (e.g. metadata.name — which is also an identity field feeding the resource id) would still ship green through this suite. Add Example rows + matching cases in givenPlanChangesImmutableField for metadata.name, install_root, and role_name so every DESIGN §5.2 immutable path is actually asserted.
